steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Grease a 9x13-inch pan.

In a large bowl, mix together oats, cake mix, and melted margarine so that it makes nice clumps and there is no dry mix left. Press 1/2 of oats mixture evenly into the bottom of the prepared pan. In a separate bowl, mix jam with water, and spread over oat mixture in the pan. Sprinkle remaining oat mixture evenly over top.
Bake in the preheated oven for 18 to 23 minutes, or until top is lightly browned. Cool before cutting into bars.

raw_recipe.headline: Raspberry Oatmeal Bars
raw_recipe.description: This recipe is quick and easy, but the resulting oatmeal bar cookies topped with raspberry jam taste so decadent.

review.reviewBody: I love these! I've made these a dozen times and here are a couple suggestions that I've found make them even better: As another user suggested, use 1 Tbsp lemon juice instead of the 1 Tbsp water. Also, I always add a few splashes of milk or evaporated milk of half and half (whatever I have on hand)to the cake mixture. It makes the bars stick together much better and they don't come out too crumbly at all.

These were really good and easy to tailor to your tastes or what you have on hand. I had a spiced cake mix that was going out of date & needed to be used. I was running low on butter so used 1/2 c butter and 1/4 c canola oil and also added 1 cup chopped, toasted walnuts and 1/2 tsp almond extract. The dough was so good that I was nibbling on it raw.

one tip is to heat you jam in the microwave for maybe 20 seconds and stir it up good so that it is easier to spread. Since jam is pretty sweet and it only made a thin later, I decided to add a single layer of frozen mixed berries. I had to bake them an extra 8-10 minutes but they turned out perfect! The berries really helped give them a more natural fruit flavor even with using a box mix and jar or jam.

 I would make these again in a heartbeat and vary the flavor. My coworkers love Nutella & I’d love to try that as a filling in these to bring to the office

Super easy tasty treat that I made the day before I served them. Followed a number of reviewer suggestions: used Duncan Hines French Vanilla (white) cake mix, added 1/2 t Vanilla, 1/2 t Almond Extract, 1 and 1/2 T Milk and substituted fresh lemon juice for the 2T water. Used Rasberry Preserves instead of jam. Used the entire jar which was a little less than 1 and 3/4 cups. Started checking doneness @ 20 minutes.....took out of oven around 26 minutes. Everyone raved and went back for seconds (and thirds!). Definitely a keeper.

Everyone loved these bars & they were so easy to make. I needed something quick & this recipe definitely fit the bill! I made only minor changes to the recipe; I used an extra 1/2 cup of jam & instead of water, I added 1.5 tablespoons of non-dairy creamer to the jam. I microwaved the jam for 30 seconds (as another poster suggested) & mixed in the non-dairy creamer after that. I did have to bake them for 27 minutes & they came out perfect. I usually use my convection oven but I was baking something else in it at the time so I used my regular oven for the bars. Next time, I will use my convection oven & adjust the time to around five minutes less.

These bars are so easy and delicious. I have made them twice, once with a butter cake mix and once with yellow, the butter turned out much better, I also, like some other reviewers, added a bit of milk to the mix after separating it into the bottom part and the top part. I didn't find it too sweet, perhaps this is because I used a reduced sugar raspberry jam from Trader Joe's and then sprinkled a few chocolate chips on top of the jam. I made it in a tart pan the first time and liked the result better than the suggested square pan. Cut into wedges and it is actually pretty elegant looking and certainly tastes homemade.

Okay- I truly screwed up this recipe, and it still turned out great, just different than the original seemed to be. Rather than 3/4 C butter, I used 1/2 C applesauce and 1/4 canola oil, plus 1/2 C egg substitute. Also, I then spread 3/4 of the mixture in the bottom of a jellyroll pan, topped with jam and lemon juice, then dropped the remaining cake mix mixture in heaping teaspoons. It came out very cakey but great, and I drizzled a lemon icing that was simply made with lemon juice and powdered sugar as soon as they came out of the oven. The result tastes a great deal like raspberry danish!

Quick, easy and delicious. I used 1/4 cup margarine and 1/2 cup unsweetened applesauce in place of the 3/4 cup margine called for. According to other suggestions, I also used lemon juice instead of water and added 1/2 teaspoon each of vanilla and almond extract. The amount of jam is perfect and more would be too much. I used a small piece of wax paper to help press the mixture into the bottom of the pan. After one hour at work, the pan was half gone and I had requests for the recipe. Try it!
Big hit , I substituted fresh raspberries with a tablespoon of cornstarch for the preserves.

just made these with a few changes, they are delicous even warm, just a tad too sweet. I took out 1/2 cup of the white cake mix and replaced with oats, add a large handlful of chopped walnuts to the mix and took out about 2/3rd and added 1 egg, 1 TBS milk, 1 tsp vanilla to bottom mix. Spread low sugear apricot butter and a handful of choc chips and put on remaining topping, baked for 28 minutes, they came out great!!

I used unsalted butter and Bonne Maman four fruit preserves (straight from the jar, no water added) and these were delicious. They are so easy to make that I feel a little guilty for not putting more effort into them. My husband loves them.

I made some for a vegan friend using Duncan Hines classic yellow cake mix and Fleischman's unsalted margarine (sticks). They aren't exactly health food but they were free of animal products and satisfied her sweet tooth.

I've also made batches using Hero blueberry and Hero strawberry fruit spread, 12 oz jar, and it's the perfect size for this recipe. It saves getting a measuring cup dirty. I didn't add any water to the fruit spread, it doesn't need it.
So easy and fast to put together! I whisked an egg into the melted butter before combing with the dry ingredients. The cookies held together nicely. Thank you for the recipe.
I used strawberry supreme cake mix and 1 1/2 jars of my home canned strawberry jam. Very yummy!
Quick, easy, and delicious. Crowd pleaser!
I used Polaner raspberry jelly. I used a pineapple cake mix and they were so tasty, became addicting.

I added peanut butter (thinned with warm water) to the oatmeal mixture when topping these. Next batch I added PB mixture into the marmalade mixture to make a thick filling. Nutmeg. Ginger, cinnamon all enhance the oat mix and varies depending on preserves chosen , fun recipe to tweak

This was a "using what I have" dessert and was a hit! I used a box butter cake because that is what I had, and used butter rather than margarine, and the buttery flavor was epic! I also used a couple more ounces of raspberry jam than the recipe , and that worked out well. I gave them a full 25 minutes and they were perfect.
Really good flavor but they fell apart. Read reviews for tips
I have made this for part of my holiday sweets for about 10 years. My family loves them. I also use Lemon juice instead of water.
